title: I revived a dead Flash game for mobile with AI (0 manual code)
author: unknownuchiha
selftext:
I’ve been building a mobile game called Ninja Horizon, inspired by a Flash game called Ninja Saga that I played a lot growing up.

The game was built entirely with AI. I started with Claude and later moved to Codex. I haven’t manually written a single line of code myself.

For the client, AI helped build the game in React Native and TypeScript. It also helped me understand the old ActionScript battle engine, rebuild the combat logic, and figure out how to run and control SWF animations using Ruffle.

For the backend, I connected AI to Supabase through MCP. It was able to work with the database, migrations, authentication, Edge Functions and multiplayer systems directly. This was also useful when debugging PvP or checking what actually happened during a battle.

The icons and background images I made for the game were generated with GPT. I found that it can produce pretty good results when you give it a solid reference image and keep correcting the details.

Writing zero code manually doesn’t mean the game came from one prompt. Most of my time went into explaining what I wanted, testing everything, finding bugs and getting AI to keep working on a problem when its first solution was wrong.

The game is now in closed beta on Android, and I’ll include some gameplay footage with this post.

If anyone wants to test it, talk about how it was built or follow the development, you can join the Discord.

[https://discord.gg/uVfUPmeju](https://discord.gg/uVfUPmeju)
